climate.overview_html: August 28’s three-story climate frame: NOAA CPC’s August update confirms the developing super El Niño is tracking toward historic strength, with Niño 3.4 already at +2.7°C and a 69% model probability of the Regional Oceanic Niño Index exceeding +2.5°C during the October–December peak — a threshold that would set an all-time El Niño record. The El Niño signal is manifesting simultaneously in two fire emergencies: Europe’s EFFIS-confirmed burnt area jumped 24% in a single week to 626,818 hectares from 1,797 fires, tracking 33% ahead of the record-setting 2025 season pace as a Copernicus drought-alert footprint covers 50% of EU+UK territory. In Southeast Asia, Indonesia has now deployed 30 fire-suppression aircraft — its largest aerial response since the catastrophic 2015 El Niño season — as peatland fires drive cross-border haze across Malaysia and respiratory risk for 3.4 million people. The triple convergence of record ocean heat, record El Niño forcing, and concurrent continental-scale fire emergencies on two separate landmasses is without historical precedent in the instrumental record.

items.headline: CPC/IRI August ENSO Update: Super El Niño at +2.7°C Niño 3.4 Anomaly; 95% Probability of Very-Strong OND Peak; 69% Model Odds of RONI ≥+2.5°C Potentially Breaking All Prior Records
items.summary: NOAA’s Climate Prediction Center August ENSO diagnostic discussion confirms the Niño 3.4 index has reached +2.7°C, already in super-El Niño territory (≥+2.0°C). The CPC/IRI plume assigns 95% probability to an Oceanic Niño Index ≥+2.0°C during the October–December 2026 peak — the threshold for “very strong” El Niño — and a 69% probability that the Regional Oceanic Niño Index (RONI) will reach or exceed +2.5°C, a level not observed in the 1950–present instrumental record. The NOAA GFDL SPEAR model’s experimental ensemble of 30 members is unanimous in projecting record El Niño strength, while the UK Met Office and ECMWF seasonal systems independently corroborate. Watchers.news notes that a confirmed RONI ≥+2.5°C would require a formal WMO exceptional-El-Niño designation and would project global average temperature anomalies in 2027 well above any year yet recorded. The August SST record of 21.1°C (set August 22, confirmed by Copernicus C3S) is directly attributable to the convergence of super El Niño forcing and the decadal anthropogenic ocean-warming trend.

items.headline: Europe Wildfire Crisis Surges 24% in One Week: EFFIS at 626,818 ha From 1,797 Fires — 33% Ahead of Record-2025 Pace; Danube Critically Low; Hungary’s Paks Nuclear Output Curtailed by Cooling-Water Temperature
items.summary: JRC EFFIS data updated through August 25 show EU-wide total burnt area has jumped from 505,683 hectares to 626,818 hectares — a 24% increase in approximately one week, sourced from 1,797 individual fire events. The EU+UK total is tracking 33% ahead of the same date in 2025, which itself reached 1,034,552 ha at season-end and set a record. Very-extreme fire-danger indices persist across the Romania–Hungary belt, with extreme danger extending to southern Ireland and central-southern Italy. The Copernicus European Drought Observatory simultaneously documents warning-to-alert-level drought across approximately half of EU+UK territory: the Danube is running at critically low levels, and Hungary’s Paks Nuclear Power Plant has been forced to reduce electrical output because Danube cooling-water temperatures have exceeded permitted discharge limits. The combined fire/drought signal is consistent with the atmospheric blocking pattern sustaining the Eastern Europe heat anomaly under El Niño-amplified northern-hemispheric circulation.

items.headline: Indonesia Worst Wildfire Season Since 2015: 30 Suppression Aircraft Deployed — Nation’s Largest Aerial Response in 11 Years; BMKG Links Peatland Drought to Super El Niño >+2.0°C ONI
items.summary: Indonesia’s National Disaster Management Agency BNPB has deployed 30 fire-suppression and cloud-seeding aircraft across Sumatra and Kalimantan — the largest aerial response the country has mounted since the catastrophic 2015 El Niño fire season, which burned 2.6 million hectares and produced Southeast Asia’s worst recorded haze event. Eco-Business reports BNPB and BMKG are explicitly linking 2026’s fire escalation to the developing super El Niño: the ONI is already above +2.0°C and tracking toward +2.5°C, reproducing the rainfall-deficit conditions that preconditioned 2015’s peatland fire catastrophe. With approximately 285,000 hectares burned and 3.4 million people at respiratory risk as of August 27, Indonesian authorities are working with Malaysian counterparts on transboundary cloud-seeding operations; Malaysia has closed 600 schools in Sarawak and suspended outdoor events ahead of National Day on August 31. BMKG warns the below-normal rainfall regime will likely persist through at least early September.

major_events.name: Typhoon Saudel — Double Landfall on Zhejiang Coast Aug 28; Yuhuan 8:05 AM (35 m/s), Wenzhou 9:10 AM (33 m/s); 100–500 mm Rainfall; 197 Flights Grounded; Shanghai Supply Chain Disrupted
major_events.status: POST-LANDFALL · FLOODING ONGOING · 100–500 MM RAINFALL · SHANGHAI DISRUPTED
major_events.impact: Typhoon Saudel made double landfall on the Zhejiang coast on the morning of August 28: first in Yuhuan county at 8:05 AM CST (sustained winds 35 m/s, Category 1 equivalent) and a second landfall in Wenzhou city at 9:10 AM CST (sustained 33 m/s) as the center tracked northwestward. CMA issued the highest-level typhoon red alert for coastal Zhejiang and Fujian. Forecast rainfall of 100–500 mm across the region has produced significant flooding on soils already saturated by Typhoon Narra’s passage three days earlier. Chinese aviation authorities grounded 197 flights at affected airports; Shanghai port operations and rail logistics are disrupted as the storm’s circulation extends north. Emergency responders are prioritizing river flooding in Wenzhou, Taizhou, and Ningbo lowlands where historical flood depths have exceeded 2 meters in comparable events.

major_events.name: US South/Southwest Heat Dome — Easing Gradually; Death Valley ~116°F; Extreme Heat Warning Through 8 PM Local; First Signs of Pattern Breakdown Emerging
major_events.status: EASING GRADUALLY · DEATH VALLEY ~116°F · EXTREME HEAT WARNING THROUGH 8 PM
major_events.impact: The US South and Southwest heat dome is showing the first credible signs of pattern breakdown on August 28, with Death Valley forecast near 116°F (47°C) — a notable drop from the near-126°F readings earlier this week — and NWS extreme heat warnings scaling back from the peak geographic extent. AccuWeather and Fox Weather both note that a weakening of the upper-level ridge is beginning over the western US, though above-normal temperatures will persist across Texas, the southern Plains, and the Desert Southwest through early September. Dallas recorded its 27th day at or above 100°F in August; the city is on pace to break its all-time August heat record. The partial easing does not signal end of the heat emergency: the overnight lows across much of the region remain in the 85–90°F range, preventing physiological recovery, and the cumulative heat stress index since August 1 remains the highest in the Lower 48 observational record.

major_events.name: BC Bald Range Wildfire — Transitioning to Mop-Up; Structure Protection Demobilized; Emergency Support Services Ending Aug 28; 6 Orders and 10 Alerts Still Active
major_events.status: MOP-UP PHASE · STRUCTURE PROTECTION DEMOBILIZED · 6 ORDERS · 10 ALERTS ACTIVE
major_events.impact: The BC Bald Range wildfire near Summerland is transitioning to mop-up phase as of August 28. BC Wildfire Service has demobilized structure-protection equipment from perimeter assignments, and the provincial emergency support services operation is concluding today. Six evacuation orders and ten evacuation alerts remain active across Summerland, Peachland, and surrounding communities, meaning residents of the most at-risk zones cannot yet return. The fire has burned approximately 25,000 hectares since its August 7 ignition; one fatality was confirmed on August 27 when an 80-year-old woman died while evacuating from Meadow Valley. Smoke continues to affect air quality across northern Washington, Idaho, and Montana, though smoke columns are no longer exhibiting the pyroconvective behavior that marked peak fire intensity earlier this week.

major_events.name: Indonesia Wildfire/Haze Emergency — 285,000 ha Burned; 3.4M at Respiratory Risk; 30 Suppression Aircraft Deployed; Malaysia Haze Persists
major_events.status: ONGOING · 285,000 HA · 30 AIRCRAFT DEPLOYED · WORST SINCE 2015
major_events.impact: Indonesia’s wildfire and haze emergency continues into August 28 with approximately 285,000 hectares burned and 3.4 million people at respiratory risk across Sumatra and Kalimantan. BNPB has deployed 30 suppression and cloud-seeding aircraft — the nation’s largest aerial response since 2015 — while coordinating cross-border cloud-seeding operations in Malaysian Sarawak airspace. Malaysia’s air quality remains degraded across multiple cities; 600 schools in Sarawak remain closed and Malaysia is monitoring whether to cancel National Day celebrations on August 31. Indonesian meteorological agency BMKG warns the peatland drought conditions enabling rapid fire spread are expected to persist through at least early September under super El Niño forcing.

major_events.name: Atlantic Basin — Invest 92L at 70% Development Odds; Possible Tropical Storm Dolly Near Bermuda at 40%; Atlantic Season Breaking Its August Quiet Streak
major_events.status: INVEST 92L 70% · POSSIBLE DOLLY 40% NEAR BERMUDA · LATE-AUGUST AWAKENING
major_events.impact: The Atlantic basin’s late-August disturbance field has intensified significantly since the August 27 digest. NHC has assigned a 70% 5-day development probability to Invest 92L, and a separate area near Bermuda carries 40% odds of producing a tropical depression or storm that could be designated Dolly — the fourth name on the 2026 Atlantic list. The upgrade reflects a temporary window of reduced El Niño wind shear over portions of the western Atlantic. Forecasters are watching a 3–5 day development window before the next El Niño-driven shear pulse is expected to re-suppress the MDR. The Atlantic has so far produced only two named storms (Alberta and Carlos) in 2026, consistent with NOAA’s below-normal season forecast, but late-August and September remain climatologically the peak of Atlantic tropical activity.

major_events.name: Europe Fire/Drought Emergency — 626,818 ha Burned EU-Wide (+24% in One Week); Danube Critically Low; Paks Nuclear Output Cut by Cooling-Water Limits
major_events.status: ONGOING · 626,818 HA · UP 24% · DROUGHT ALERT ACROSS 50% EU+UK
major_events.impact: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area has surged from 505,683 to 626,818 hectares in approximately one week — a 24% jump consistent with accelerating fire activity across Eastern Europe, southern Ireland, and central Italy. Very-extreme fire danger indices from JRC cover the Romania–Hungary corridor; extreme danger persists over southern Ireland and much of central-southern Italy. The Copernicus European Drought Observatory documents warning-to-alert-level drought across 50% of EU+UK territory: the Danube is running at critically low stage, and Hungary’s Paks Nuclear Power Plant is curtailing output because Danube cooling-water temperatures exceed permitted thermal-discharge limits. The 2026 fire season is tracking 33% ahead of the same date in 2025, which itself finished as the worst European fire season in the modern satellite record at 1,034,552 ha.

major_events.name: Pakistan Monsoon Flooding — Toll ≥126 Since June 26; Heavy-Rain Pulses Continuing Across Punjab, KP, Sindh
major_events.status: ONGOING · FLASH FLOODING · PUNJAB / KP / SINDH
major_events.impact: Pakistan’s cumulative monsoon death toll since June 26 stands at or above 126 per PDMA reports, with PMD continuing to issue heavy-rain advisories for successive pulses affecting northern and central Pakistan. Flash flooding across Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Sindh districts has inundated agricultural land, damaged infrastructure, and displaced tens of thousands. The 2026 monsoon is tracking as one of the more damaging of the decade in Pakistan, though not on the scale of the catastrophic 2022 season. PMD flags further heavy-rain risk in the coming days as the monsoon trough maintains an active position over the subcontinent.

weather.overview_html: August 28’s dominant weather story: Typhoon Saudel made double landfall on the Zhejiang coast — Yuhuan at 8:05 AM CST (35 m/s) and Wenzhou at 9:10 AM CST (33 m/s), driving 100–500 mm rainfall across soils already saturated by Typhoon Narra three days earlier; 197 flights were grounded and Shanghai supply chains disrupted. On the US side, the heat dome is showing the first signs of pattern breakdown with Death Valley near 116°F, a notable pullback from the near-126°F readings earlier this week though above-normal heat will persist into early September. The BC Bald Range wildfire has transitioned to mop-up phase with structure protection demobilized and emergency services winding down, though six orders and ten alerts remain active. The Atlantic is showing its late-August awakening: Invest 92L is now at 70% development odds with a separate area near Bermuda carrying 40% odds of producing possible Tropical Storm Dolly, marking the basin’s most active disturbance field since early August.

items.headline: Typhoon Saudel Double Landfall on Zhejiang: Yuhuan 8:05 AM CST (35 m/s), Wenzhou 9:10 AM CST (33 m/s); 100–500 mm Rainfall; 197 Flights Grounded; Flooding Across Saturated Coastal Lowlands
items.summary: Typhoon Saudel completed a double landfall on China’s Zhejiang coast on the morning of August 28. CMA confirmed the first landfall in Yuhuan county at 8:05 AM China Standard Time with maximum sustained winds of 35 m/s (approximately 68 kt, equivalent to Category 1 on the Saffir-Simpson scale); the center then moved to a second landfall in Wenzhou city at 9:10 AM CST with sustained winds of 33 m/s as the storm weakened slightly over land. Forecast rainfall of 100–500 mm across the Wenzhou–Taizhou–Ningbo corridor is falling on soils already saturated by Typhoon Narra’s passage three days earlier, dramatically amplifying flash-flood and river-flood potential. Aviation authorities grounded 197 flights at regional airports; Shanghai’s port operations and freight logistics are disrupted. Emergency rescue teams were pre-positioned across Wenzhou, Taizhou, and Ningbo ahead of landfall.

items.headline: US Heat Dome Begins Easing: Death Valley Near 116°F on Aug 28 Versus Near-126°F Earlier This Week; NWS Scales Back Warning Area; Above-Normal Temperatures Persist Into Early September
items.summary: The US South and Southwest heat dome that produced near-126°F readings in Death Valley and shattered records across 27 states is showing the first credible signs of weakening on August 28. Death Valley is forecast near 116°F (47°C) — still extreme but meaningfully below the week’s peak. NWS has narrowed the geographic extent of active extreme heat warnings, and AccuWeather forecasters identify an emerging ridge-breakdown signal in the medium-range ensemble. Dallas registered its 27th day at or above 100°F in August 2026, still on pace to break the all-time August record. Fox Weather cautions that above-normal temperatures will persist across the southern US through at least early September and that the overnight low temperatures — remaining in the 85–90°F range in many cities — continue to pose the highest physiological risk, especially for elderly residents without air conditioning.

items.headline: BC Bald Range Wildfire Enters Mop-Up Phase: Structure Protection Demobilized; Emergency Support Ending Aug 28; 6 Evacuation Orders and 10 Alerts Remain Active Around Summerland and Peachland
items.summary: The Bald Range wildfire near Summerland, BC — which claimed one life on August 27 when an 80-year-old woman died while fleeing Meadow Valley — is transitioning to mop-up operations as of August 28. BC Wildfire Service has demobilized heavy structure-protection equipment from perimeter assignments, signaling that active structural threat has substantially diminished. The province’s emergency support services operation serving displaced residents is closing today. However, six evacuation orders and ten evacuation alerts remain active, meaning residents of the highest-risk zones adjacent to the fire perimeter cannot yet return home. The fire has burned approximately 25,000 hectares across the Summerland–Peachland corridor since its August 7 ignition. Air quality alerts from smoke continue to affect northern Washington, Idaho, and Montana, though pyroconvective activity that drove extreme behavior earlier this week has subsided with the easing of the heat dome.

items.headline: Atlantic Late-August Awakening: Invest 92L Upgraded to 70% Development Odds; Separate Area Near Bermuda at 40% for Possible Tropical Storm Dolly; Most Active Disturbance Field Since Early August
items.summary: The Atlantic basin’s disturbance field has intensified sharply since yesterday’s digest. NHC has upgraded Invest 92L — a system that was Invest 96L at 20–40% odds in the August 27 digest before being redesignated as it moved — to a 70% 5-day development probability as the system tracks through a window of temporarily reduced El Niño-driven wind shear. A separate, independent tropical disturbance near Bermuda now carries 40% development odds and could become Tropical Storm Dolly, the fourth named storm of the 2026 Atlantic season. Meteorologists note the late-August timing is climatologically consistent with the peak of Atlantic tropical activity (statistically centered on September 10), and that even one organized storm would represent a breakout from the El Niño-suppressed baseline that has held the Atlantic quiet since July. NOAA’s below-normal 2026 season forecast remains in effect.

renewables.overview_html: Three data points solidify the structural picture of global clean energy deployment. In India, ACME Solar secured $164 million (₹1,571 crore) in IIFCL financing for a 300 MW Rajasthan solar + 1,350 MWh battery storage project — one of the largest BESS co-deployments announced in India this year, underpinned by the government-owned infrastructure lender. In the US, Environment America’s analysis of EIA data confirms US wind and solar reached 22% of national electricity generation in H1 2026, with June 2026 marking the first month in US history in which solar generation exceeded wind — a technological and economic milestone. The updated 22% figure surpasses the 20% H1 headline from August 20, reflecting a more detailed disaggregated analysis. And CleanTechnica’s structural analysis documents why US renewable energy deployment has continued accelerating despite federal policy headwinds: the forces driving installation — falling costs, long-term utility contracts, and state-level policy certainty — are now decoupled from federal incentives that have been curtailed or threatened.

items.headline: ACME Solar Secures ₹1,571 Crore ($164M) IIFCL Financing for 300 MW Rajasthan Solar + 1,350 MWh Battery Storage Project — One of India’s Largest BESS Co-Deployments of 2026
items.summary: ACME Solar Holdings has secured ₹1,571 crore (approximately $164 million USD) in infrastructure debt financing from IIFCL (India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited), the government-owned institution that provides long-tenor project finance for strategic infrastructure, for a hybrid renewable energy project in Rajasthan. The project combines 300 MW of utility-scale solar PV with 1,350 MWh of co-located battery energy storage — a 4.5-hour storage ratio that qualifies as long-duration for Indian grid purposes. At 1,350 MWh, the BESS component is among the largest single-site battery deployments announced in India in 2026. The IIFCL financing signals that India’s sovereign infrastructure lenders are scaling up hybrid renewable project support, consistent with the government’s target of 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030 and the Ministry of Power’s emphasis on round-the-clock renewable supply for industrial consumers.

items.headline: US Wind + Solar Reach 22% of National Generation in H1 2026; June 2026 Marks First Month Solar Exceeds Wind in US History — Updated EIA Analysis Surpasses Earlier 20% Headline
items.summary: Environment America’s disaggregated analysis of EIA generation data confirms that US wind and solar collectively produced 22% of total national electricity generation in the first half of 2026 — a revision above the 20% H1 figure from MarketScale’s earlier reporting, reflecting more complete utility and distributed-generation data. The more significant data point within the report: June 2026 is the first calendar month in US history in which solar generation (utility-scale plus distributed) exceeded wind generation on an energy basis, marking a structural inflection in the US generation mix. Solar’s seasonal advantage in summer months, combined with the cumulative installation base now exceeding 350 GW, has crossed the threshold where it can lead the renewables fleet even against the installed wind base. The Environment America analysis also notes that combined wind, solar, and hydropower generation exceeded 30% of US supply in H1 2026, with hydropower serving as a seasonally variable firm complement.

items.headline: Renewable Energy’s Structural Wins: Why US Solar, Wind, and Storage Deployment Is Accelerating Despite Federal Policy Headwinds — Falling Costs, Long-Term Contracts, and State Policy Form a Resilient Tripod
items.summary: CleanTechnica’s analysis examines the paradox at the core of the 2026 US energy picture: federal policy has consistently attempted to slow clean energy deployment through tariff escalation on solar components, incentive rollbacks, and permitting obstacles, yet utility-scale solar, wind, and battery storage installations are continuing to accelerate. The piece identifies three self-reinforcing mechanisms that have decoupled deployment from federal support: (1) capital cost curves for solar and lithium-ion storage that have fallen far enough that new projects are economical without federal production tax credits in most Sun Belt markets; (2) long-term power purchase agreements signed between 2022 and 2025 that lock in project economics regardless of subsequent policy changes; and (3) state-level renewable portfolio standards and clean energy standards in 30+ states that create demand certainty for developers. The analysis notes that H1 2026’s 22% wind+solar generation share arrived despite, not because of, the current federal posture — and that data center and industrial load growth are creating a new PPA demand pool that accelerates the economics further.

science.overview_html: Three results bracket the digest’s physical-science context. Most immediately operationally relevant: NOAA GFDL’s SPEAR model experimental August ENSO prediction — all 30 ensemble members projecting record El Niño strength at ONI peak — now informs real-time hazard planning for the Indonesia, Europe, and US West heat emergencies that dominate this week’s digest. On the climate-trend side, Foster & Rahmstorf in Geophysical Research Letters document that global warming has measurably accelerated since approximately 2015: a quadratic trend of +0.036°C per decade per decade is statistically significant at >98% confidence across four of five major global mean surface temperature datasets, placing the current warming rate at roughly double the mid-20th-century baseline. Bridging hazard and response: Google DeepMind open-sourced the WeatherNext family of AI weather models — including WeatherNext Cyclones, validated at a 24-hour track-error advantage over ensemble NWP for tropical cyclones, and co-developed with NOAA’s National Hurricane Center, CIRA, and the UK Met Office — published in Nature under an Apache 2.0 license. WeatherNext Cyclones’ performance was directly tested against Typhoon Saudel as forecasters evaluated its track guidance alongside operational NWP.

items.headline: NOAA GFDL SPEAR August Experimental ENSO Forecast: All 30 Ensemble Members Project Record El Niño Strength at OND 2026 Peak — Unanimous Signal Supports CPC’s 95% Very-Strong Probability
items.meta: NOAA GFDL SPEAR model · August 2026 experimental ENSO prediction · 30-member ensemble
items.summary: NOAA’s Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Laboratory released its experimental August 2026 El Niño prediction from the SPEAR (Seamless System for Prediction and Earth System Research) coupled climate model. The result is striking in its unanimity: all 30 ensemble members project Niño 3.4 at or above the +2.5°C level during the October–December 2026 peak, with the ensemble mean tracking near +2.8°C and several members reaching +3.0°C or higher. This unanimity is statistically uncommon in seasonal El Niño prediction — typically a fraction of ensemble members project opposing phase outcomes. The GFDL result is consistent with and independently corroborates the CPC’s dynamical-model consensus of ≥95% probability for a very-strong (ONI ≥+2.0°C) event. SPEAR’s coupled ocean-atmosphere dynamics capture the current anomalous warmth in the eastern Pacific, the anomalous westerly wind bursts that have reinforced positive Kelvin wave forcing since June, and the thermocline shoaling that precludes a rebound to neutral conditions. Operational weather and climate services globally are using SPEAR guidance to inform multi-month hazard outlooks for the 2026–27 fire, drought, and flood seasons.

items.headline: Foster & Rahmstorf GRL: Global Warming Has Measurably Accelerated Since ~2015 — Quadratic Trend of +0.036°C/Decade² Significant at >98% Confidence in 4 of 5 GMST Datasets
items.meta: G. Foster, S. Rahmstorf · Geophysical Research Letters · vol. 53(5) · DOI: 10.1029/2025GL118804
items.summary: Grant Foster and Stefan Rahmstorf present a quantitative analysis of global mean surface temperature (GMST) acceleration in Geophysical Research Letters. Fitting a quadratic (linearly accelerating) trend to five major GMST datasets — NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GlobalTemp, Berkeley Earth, HadCRUT5, and ERA5 — the authors find a statistically significant acceleration of approximately +0.036°C per decade per decade since approximately 2015 in four of the five datasets. The acceleration is significant at more than 98% confidence in those four datasets. At the current warming rate, which the quadratic fit places near +0.25°C per decade, global average temperature is tracking toward 2.0°C above pre-industrial levels before 2050 absent aggressive emissions reduction. The authors stress the physical mechanisms behind acceleration: continued greenhouse forcing from record 2023–2026 atmospheric CO&sub2; concentrations, reduced cooling from shipping-sector sulfate aerosol emission cuts since 2020, and the positive feedback contribution of declining Arctic sea-ice albedo. The paper has drawn substantial attention as 2026 is on pace to be the hottest year in the instrumental record by a wide margin.

items.headline: Google DeepMind Open-Sources WeatherNext Family: WeatherNext Cyclones Achieves +24-Hour TC Track Advantage Over Ensemble NWP; Co-Developed With NHC, CIRA, UK Met Office; Published in Nature; Apache 2.0
items.meta: Google DeepMind & Google Research, co-developed with NOAA NHC, CIRA, UK Met Office · Nature · August 2026 · Apache 2.0 license
items.summary: Google DeepMind released WeatherNext, a family of AI weather and tropical cyclone forecasting models, as open-source software under the Apache 2.0 license, with accompanying research published in Nature. The WeatherNext family comprises three distinct systems: WeatherNext Cyclones, a specialized tropical cyclone track-and-intensity model co-developed with NOAA’s National Hurricane Center, the Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere (CIRA), and the UK Met Office; WeatherNext 2, a global medium-range weather model; and WeatherNext 2-mini, a computationally efficient variant. The headline result for WeatherNext Cyclones: it achieves a statistically significant 24-hour track error advantage over leading ensemble NWP systems in held-out validation on Atlantic, East Pacific, and Western Pacific basins. The co-development with operational forecast centers — NOAA NHC and the UK Met Office among them — is notable because it embeds operational knowledge directly into training objectives, rather than benchmarking a research model against operational output. The Nature publication provides full architecture details and training methodology. WeatherNext Cyclones’ guidance was available to forecasters tracking Typhoon Saudel during its Zhejiang landfall on August 28, providing the first live operational test of a Nature-published AI cyclone model against a major landfalling typhoon.

items.title: Mantel Capture Raises $18M Series A Extension From Constellation Technology Ventures and Azimut — Brings Total Funding to $50M; MIT Chemical Engineering Spinout Scales Molten-Borate Liquid-Phase Carbon Capture for Heavy Industry
items.body_html: Mantel Capture raised an $18 million strategic extension to its Series A on August 24, 2026, led by Constellation Technology Ventures (the venture arm of Constellation Energy, the largest US nuclear operator) with co-investment from Azimut, the Milan-based alternative asset manager. The extension brings Mantel’s total funding to approximately $50 million. The company, spun out of MIT’s Department of Chemical Engineering, is developing a molten-borate liquid-phase carbon capture process designed for industrial point sources — cement kilns, steel blast furnaces, and chemical manufacturing — where the high-temperature, high-CO&sub2;-concentration exhaust streams make Mantel’s chemistry more efficient than amine-scrubbing alternatives. Constellation Technology Ventures’ participation is strategically significant: it signals that Constellation’s nuclear fleet, which generates large amounts of firm low-carbon electricity, may serve as a preferred power source for energy-intensive electrochemical carbon-capture operations. Azimut’s entry provides a European distribution channel as EU industrial decarbonization mandates under the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism create demand for verified hard-to-abate-sector CO&sub2; removal.
items.source_html: GlobeNewswire / ESG Today

items.title: Boldr Raises $5M Pre-Series A From Unconventional Ventures, Ada Ventures, and Inclimo Climate Tech Fund — HVAC-to-Virtual-Power-Plant Demand Flexibility Platform Targets Grid-Capacity Markets
items.body_html: Boldr closed a $5 million (€4.2 million) pre-Series A funding round on August 24, 2026, led by Unconventional Ventures with participation from Ada Ventures, Inclimo Climate Tech Fund, and strategic angels from the European grid and proptech sector. Boldr’s platform converts residential HVAC systems — heat pumps, air conditioning units, and underfloor heating — into demand-flexibility resources enrolled in virtual power plants (VPP), allowing grid operators to curtail or shift heating and cooling loads in response to grid frequency signals and balancing market prices. Homeowners receive financial compensation through grid-service revenue sharing. The business model targets the gap between distributed energy resources (DERs) already installed in European homes and the VPP aggregation infrastructure needed to monetize that latent grid capacity: European regulators under ENTSO-E framework changes effective 2025 now require TSOs to source a larger share of balancing reserves from demand-side resources. Inclimo’s participation signals that dedicated climate-tech funds are moving into grid-services infrastructure plays at the pre-Series A stage.
items.source_html: Tech.eu / PropTech Connect

items.title: TotalEnergies Acquires Shell’s Entire European Onshore Renewables Business (4 GW: 500 MW Operating + 3.5 GW Pipeline) Then Sells 50% Stake in 1.2 GW Portfolio to KKR at €1.8B Enterprise Value
items.body_html: TotalEnergies announced on August 3 that it had simultaneously agreed to acquire Shell’s entire European onshore renewables portfolio and sell a 50% stake in a 1.2 GW sub-portfolio to KKR, in a paired transaction that consolidates TotalEnergies’ position as Europe’s largest independent renewable energy company while recycling capital through the KKR co-investment. The Shell acquisition adds approximately 4 GW of European onshore wind and solar capacity across multiple Western European markets: roughly 500 MW of operating assets generating current revenue and a 3.5 GW development pipeline in advanced permitting. The simultaneous KKR co-investment at an enterprise value of €1.8 billion for the 1.2 GW sub-portfolio implies an asset value of approximately €1,500/kW for developed European onshore renewables — a reference data point for the sector. The structure allows TotalEnergies to fund the Shell acquisition partially through the KKR proceeds rather than purely from its balance sheet, and gives KKR immediate exposure to operating and near-ready assets without taking development-stage risk. Shell’s exit from European onshore renewables — one of the higher-profile reversals in its 2025–2026 strategic restructuring — stands in contrast to TotalEnergies’ continued scale-up.
items.source_html: TotalEnergies Newsroom / Euronews / Yahoo Finance Energy
